ios.moderation.empty.description: You haven't blocked anyone or filed a report, and your server hasn't acted on your account.
ios.moderation.empty.title: Nothing to Show
ios.moderation.note.appeal_master_key: An appeal is confirmed with your account key, not your session — so you can appeal even when it's your account that's suspended.
ios.moderation.note.no_scanning: Your server can't look at your photos. They're sealed before they leave your device, so there's nothing to scan.
ios.moderation.note.no_silent_ops: Every action taken on your account is recorded here. Nothing happens quietly.
ios.moderation.section.audit_footer: Every action your server takes is recorded here. None of them delete your photos — they stop your server serving them, and your own copies and backups are untouched.
ios.moderation.section.blocks_footer: A blocked person is removed from albums you share with them and can't share new ones with you. What they already downloaded stays with them — nothing can reach back and take it.
ios.moderation.section.reports_footer: Reports go to whoever runs the server the content is on. Your report names the item, never its contents — nobody gains the ability to read anything by receiving it.
ios.moderation.section.untrusted: Content from Servers You Haven't Trusted
ios.moderation.section.untrusted_footer: Capsule holds content from servers you haven't trusted until you say so. Nothing is deleted while it waits.
ios.moderation.title: Blocking & Reports
ios.moderation.unblock.confirm_message: They'll be able to share albums with you again. They aren't added back to anything they were removed from.
ios.passkey.done.description: You can now sign in with this passkey instead of your password.
ios.passkey.done.title: Passkey Added
ios.passkey.name.footer: Something you'll recognize later, like the name of this device.
ios.passkey.name.label: Passkey Name
ios.passkey.scope_note: A passkey replaces your password when you sign in. It can't recover your account — only your recovery phrase can do that.
ios.passkey.subtitle: Sign in with Face ID, Touch ID, or your device passcode instead of a password.
ios.passkey.title: Add a Passkey
ios.passkey.unavailable.description: This device has nowhere to keep a passkey. Sign in with your password instead.
ios.passkey.unavailable.title: No Place to Keep a Passkey
ios.peering.enable.footer: Your devices swap photos directly over the local network, without going through your server. Useful when the server is far away or offline.
ios.peering.idle.description: Capsule is listening. Your other devices will show up when they're on the same network.
ios.peering.idle.title: Nothing Nearby
ios.peering.note.lan_only: Only over the local network. Nothing is exchanged across the internet this way.
ios.peering.note.no_scope_knob: Nearby syncing follows the same What to Sync setting as everything else — there's no separate one to set.
ios.peering.note.pull_only: Each device asks for what it's missing. Nothing is pushed at you.
ios.peering.note.same_account: Only devices signed in to your account. Someone else's device on the same network can't take part.
ios.peering.section.unpaired_footer: Capsule only exchanges photos with devices signed in to your own account.
ios.peering.title: Nearby Devices
ios.places.empty.description: Photos with location data will appear here.
ios.places.empty.title: No Places
ios.places.title: Places
ios.quarantine.action.discard.descriptio: Destroy what was kept. This can't be undone.
ios.quarantine.action.inspect.descriptio: Look at what was kept, without changing anything.
ios.quarantine.action.inspect.unavailabl: Nothing was kept to inspect — only a record that this happened.
ios.quarantine.action.repair.description: Try to put this right and return it to your library.
ios.quarantine.action.repair.unavailable: There's nothing here that repairing could fix.
ios.quarantine.detail.actions.footer: There's no default here. Capsule won't choose for you, however long this waits.
ios.quarantine.detail.title: Review Item
ios.quarantine.detail.what_is_kept.foote: Nothing here has been deleted or applied. It's waiting for you to decide.
ios.quarantine.discard.confirm.message: What was kept will be destroyed for good. The record that this happened stays in your history.
ios.quarantine.discard.confirm.title: Discard This Item?
ios.quarantine.empty.description: Anything Capsule holds back for you to look at will appear here.
ios.quarantine.empty.title: Nothing to Review
ios.quarantine.inspect.footer: The start of the kept data, shown as-is. Useful in a bug report; nothing here changes the item.
ios.quarantine.inspect.title: What Was Kept
ios.quarantine.reason.awaiting_review: This is waiting for you to accept it.
ios.quarantine.reason.awaiting_upgrade: This is waiting for its album to be upgraded.
ios.quarantine.reason.malformed: The data couldn't be read as anything Capsule understands.
ios.quarantine.reason.schema_ahead: This was written by a newer version of Capsule. It's kept exactly as it is, and this version won't change it.
ios.quarantine.reason.server_rejected: Your server refused this. The reason code is above.
ios.quarantine.reason.stale_chain: This is older than the version already in your library.
ios.quarantine.reason.verify_rejected: The signature or history on this change didn't check out.
ios.quarantine.storage.preserved: The original data was kept, so you can still get this back.
ios.quarantine.storage.recorded_only: Only a record of what happened was kept — there's no data here to recover.
ios.quarantine.surface.album_upgrade.des: This change is waiting for its album to be upgraded. It'll be applied once that's done.
ios.quarantine.surface.federation.descri: Content arrived from another server that Capsule couldn't verify, so it wasn't added.
ios.quarantine.surface.orphan.descriptio: A photo file was found with no record of what it is. The file is kept exactly as it was.
ios.quarantine.surface.pending_drop.desc: Someone uploaded this through one of your links. It's waiting for you to accept it into your library.
A backup you restored disagrees with what your library already has. Capsule held it rather than overwriting newer work.
ios.quarantine.surface.sidecar.descripti: A photo's record couldn't be read. The unreadable data is kept exactly as it was, in case it can be recovered.
ios.quarantine.surface.stale_revival.des: Something offered an older version of a photo than the one you already have. Capsule held it rather than winding your library back.
ios.quarantine.surface.unknown.descripti: A newer version of Capsule held this back for a reason this version doesn't recognize. It's kept exactly as it is.
ios.quarantine.surface.verify_reject.des: A change arrived that Capsule couldn't confirm came from a device on your account, so it wasn't applied.
ios.quarantine.title: Needs Review
ios.quota.category.trash.note: Deleted photos still count until they're purged for good.
ios.quota.empty.description: Your server hasn't reported a storage figure yet.
ios.quota.empty.title: No Storage Information
ios.quota.link.local_storage.footer: Freeing space on this device doesn't change what's stored on your server.
ios.quota.offline.notice: Offline — this is the last figure your server sent
ios.quota.state.grace_expired.descriptio: Storage has been full long enough that edits — captions, tags, new links — are paused as well. Reading, deleting, and restoring still work, and freeing space lifts this.
ios.quota.state.hard_exceeded.descriptio: New uploads are refused until you free space. Everything already stored is untouched and still readable.
ios.quota.state.soft_warning.description: Uploads still work. Freeing some space now avoids being stopped later.
ios.quota.state.suspended.description: Whoever runs this server has suspended the account. They can tell you why and what happens next.
ios.quota.state.unknown.description: Your server reported a state this version of Capsule doesn't recognize.
ios.quota.title: Server Storage
ios.quota.usage.title: Usage
ios.recently_deleted.empty.description: Deleted Capsule photos appear here for recovery.
ios.recently_deleted.empty.title: No Recently Deleted
ios.recently_deleted.title: Recently Deleted
ios.recovery.passphrase.copy_note: The clipboard is cleared as soon as this device allows. Paste it straight into your password manager.
ios.recovery.passphrase.done.description: Keep your phrase somewhere safe. You'll need it if you ever lose every device.
ios.recovery.passphrase.done.title: Recovery Is Set Up
ios.recovery.passphrase.empty.descriptio: There's no recovery phrase for this account yet.
ios.recovery.passphrase.empty.title: No Recovery Phrase
ios.recovery.passphrase.entropy.defect: Capsule generated this phrase, so this is a fault in this version of the app and not something you did. Don't rely on this phrase — report the problem and set up recovery again.
ios.recovery.passphrase.entropy.footnote: Measured in bits against the minimum Capsule requires. Anything that stores your phrase can be attacked offline, so the phrase itself has to carry the strength.
ios.recovery.passphrase.entropy.label: Phrase Strength
ios.recovery.passphrase.gate.no_skip: This step can't be skipped. A phrase nobody wrote down protects nothing.
ios.recovery.passphrase.gate.subtitle: Enter the words below to confirm you have the phrase.
ios.recovery.passphrase.gate.title: Type It Back
ios.recovery.passphrase.shown_once: This phrase is shown once. Write it down or save it somewhere safe now — nobody, including Capsule, can show it to you again.
ios.recovery.passphrase.subtitle: This phrase is the only way back into your library if you lose your devices. Write it down before you continue.
ios.recovery.passphrase.title: Your Recovery Phrase
ios.recovery.verify.badge.description: Capsule will keep showing this until you check. It still won't stop you doing anything.
ios.recovery.verify.field.footer: Typed here only to check it. It isn't sent anywhere and isn't stored.
ios.recovery.verify.field.label: Recovery Phrase
ios.recovery.verify.never_blocks: This check never blocks anything. Your library keeps working either way.
ios.recovery.verify.not_armed.descriptio: This account recovers through whoever sponsors it, so it has no phrase of its own.
ios.recovery.verify.not_armed.title: Nothing to Check
ios.recovery.verify.rewrap.description: Capsule can give you a new phrase for the same account key. Your photos aren't touched and nothing is re-encrypted.
ios.recovery.verify.rewrap.title: Set a New Recovery Phrase
ios.recovery.verify.subtitle: A quick check that the phrase you saved still works. Nothing depends on doing it now.
ios.recovery.verify.title: Check Your Recovery Phrase
ios.recovery.verify.unconfigured.descrip: There's no recovery phrase on this account yet, so there's nothing to check.
ios.recovery.verify.unconfigured.title: Recovery Not Set Up
ios.restore.commit.confirm.message: This writes the changes you just reviewed into your library. Type the phrase below to confirm.
ios.restore.commit.confirm.title: Apply This Restore?
ios.restore.commit.description: Applies everything listed above to your library.
ios.restore.commit.note: Available only after a comparison that passed its checks. You'll be asked to type a phrase to confirm.
ios.restore.commit.title: Apply the Restore
ios.restore.diff.reconciliation_note: Anything that differs is held for you to decide, never applied on its own. An old backup won't bring back a photo you deleted since.
ios.restore.dry_run.description: Compares the backup with your library and reports what restoring it would do. Still nothing is changed.
ios.restore.dry_run.title: What Would Change
ios.restore.preview.description: Reads the backup and reports what it holds. Nothing is changed.
ios.restore.preview.title: What's in the Backup
ios.restore.shamir.description: Your recovery secret can be split into shares held by different people or places. Enough of them together rebuild it; one on its own reveals nothing.
ios.restore.shamir.empty: No shares are available on this device.
ios.restore.shamir.invalidated_note: This share was replaced and no longer counts. Ask whoever holds it to destroy it, and give them the current one.
ios.restore.shamir.title: Restore from Shares
ios.restore.subtitle: Look at what's in this backup and see what it would change before anything is applied.
ios.restore.title: Restore from Backup
ios.restore.verify.refused: Capsule won't restore this backup while the checks above are failing. The file is left exactly as it is.
ios.scaffold.body: This screen is wired into navigation but has no interface yet.
ios.scaffold.title: Not built yet
ios.search.empty.title: No Matches
ios.settings.account.actions.footer: Signing out leaves your photos on this device alone. Nothing is deleted.
ios.settings.account.empty.description: Connect a server to use Capsule with an account.
ios.settings.account.empty.title: Not Signed In
ios.settings.account.identity.footer: Your handle is bound to this server. Your identity isn't — you keep it if you move.
ios.settings.account.portability.body: You can move to a different server and keep your identity, your photos, and everyone you share with.
Every device, including this one, will be signed out. You'll be asked to confirm with your account key. Your photos stay where they are.
ios.settings.account.sessions.footer: Ending one session signs out that device only. Everything else keeps working.
ios.settings.account.signout.confirm.mes: This device signs out of your server. Photos already on it stay where they are.
ios.settings.account.state.label: Session
ios.settings.account.type.label: Account Type
ios.settings.ai.empty.description: This device can't run Capsule's on-device models.
ios.settings.ai.empty.title: Not Available Here
ios.settings.ai.pending.label: Waiting to Be Analyzed
ios.settings.ai.processing.footer: Everything runs on this device. No photo and nothing derived from one is ever sent anywhere for analysis.
ios.settings.ai.provenance.body: Anything Capsule works out about a photo is kept separately from what you wrote yourself, and labelled with the model that produced it. Removing a model or redoing an analysis never touches your own edits.
ios.settings.ai.provenance.footer: Your own captions and tags are never changed by anything on this screen.
ios.settings.ai.remove.confirm.message: Features that use it stop working until you download it again. Your photos aren't affected.
ios.settings.ai.remove.confirm.title: Remove This Model?
ios.settings.ai.slot.label: Model
ios.settings.ai.slots.footer: Models download separately from the app, so you only fetch the ones you use.
ios.settings.ai.stale.footer: Results from an older version are kept but left out of searches, because results from two versions can't be compared. Redoing the analysis brings them back — nothing has been deleted.
ios.settings.appearance.density.footer: Set per device, so your Mac and your phone can differ.
ios.settings.appearance.density.label: Density
ios.settings.appearance.glass.footer: If you've turned on Reduce Transparency in the system settings, Capsule already follows it.
ios.settings.appearance.theme.footer: Following the system is usually what you want — it already knows when you prefer dark.
ios.settings.appearance.theme.label: Appearance
ios.settings.confirm.phrase.footer: Type the phrase exactly as shown. This action can't be undone.
ios.settings.diagnostics.footer: Collects crash and performance diagnostics on this device using Apple's MetricKit. Nothing leaves your device unless you turn on uploads below.
ios.settings.import.default.footer: Used whenever no rule below picks somewhere else.
ios.settings.import.default.label: Album
ios.settings.import.empty.description: Import some photos and the sources you used will be listed here.
ios.settings.import.empty.title: No Import Sources
ios.settings.import.kinds.footer: Applies to any source of that kind you haven't set an album for.
ios.settings.import.order.footer: Capsule works down this list and uses the first rule that applies. Whichever one fired is shown on every import.
ios.settings.import.rule.scope_override: A rule you set for this source
ios.settings.import.rule.source_kind_def: The default for this kind of source
ios.settings.import.sources.footer: Set an album here and imports from that source always go there, whatever the rules above would have chosen.
ios.settings.import.sources.none: You haven't imported from anywhere yet.
ios.settings.keys.cohorts.footer: Reinstalling Capsule enrolls new keys, so one device can appear more than once. Capsule groups those entries together.
ios.settings.keys.devices.footer: Revoked devices stay listed. Their keys are kept so everything they ever signed can still be checked.
ios.settings.keys.empty.description: Devices appear here once they're enrolled on your account.
ios.settings.keys.empty.title: No Devices
ios.settings.keys.enroll.footer: The code works once and expires shortly. You'll compare a safety code on both devices before anything is transferred.
ios.settings.keys.revoke.confirm.message: It can no longer read or change anything on your account. It keeps whatever it already downloaded, and everything it signed stays verifiable.
ios.settings.keys.revoke.confirm.title: Revoke This Device?
ios.settings.keys.rotation.body: Revoking a device changes the keys for every album it could reach, so it can't read anything added afterwards. Your other devices pick up the new keys on their next sync.
ios.settings.keys.rotation.footer: There's nothing to do here — this is how Capsule already behaves.
ios.settings.language.catalog.footer: Translations arrive as they're finished. Anything not yet translated is shown in English.
ios.settings.language.preferred.footer: Capsule uses the first of these it has a translation for.
ios.settings.language.resolved.footer: Capsule follows the language order in your system settings. Change it there.
ios.settings.maintenance.confirm.message: This can take a while and use a lot of battery. Capsule still waits for the right conditions — asking for it doesn't override that.
ios.settings.maintenance.confirm.title: Run This Now?
ios.settings.maintenance.dedupe.footer: Capsule only finds duplicates. Which copy to keep is always yours to choose — nothing is merged or deleted on its own.
ios.settings.maintenance.detail.cache_ev: Frees downloaded copies to stay under your cache limit. Only copies your server already holds, and they're fetched again when you need them.
ios.settings.maintenance.detail.deep_con: Re-reads every stored file to catch corruption that nothing else would notice. Slow, and wants a charger.
ios.settings.maintenance.detail.index_re: Compares Capsule's index against what's actually on this device. Quick, and reports anything that doesn't line up.
ios.settings.maintenance.detail.intra_li: Looks for the same photo stored more than once and lists what it finds. It never merges or deletes anything itself.
ios.settings.maintenance.detail.structur: Checks that each photo's record reads correctly and its signatures hold. Reasonably quick.
ios.settings.maintenance.detail.trash_pu: Permanently removes deleted photos once they're past their retention period, freeing the space they held. This one can't be undone.
ios.settings.maintenance.detail.unknown: A job a newer version of Capsule knows about and this one doesn't.
ios.settings.maintenance.empty.descripti: There's no library on this device to check yet.
ios.settings.maintenance.empty.title: Nothing to Maintain
ios.settings.maintenance.jobs.footer: Some of these are slow and want a charger. Capsule waits for the right conditions rather than running them at a bad moment.
ios.settings.maintenance.scrub.body: At most once a week, Capsule clears leftover working files from writes that were interrupted. It only touches files more than ten minutes old, and only ones nothing refers to.
ios.settings.maintenance.scrub.footer: Nothing here needs starting — this happens by itself.
ios.settings.notifications.detail.quaran: Raised when Capsule holds something back for you to look at. This can't be switched off — nothing is applied or discarded without you.
ios.settings.notifications.detail.quota: Raised when your server stops accepting uploads. This can't be switched off — uploads failing quietly is worse than being told.
ios.settings.notifications.detail.recove: Raised when it's been a while since your recovery phrase was checked. This can't be switched off — a phrase nobody has checked is one you find out about at the worst moment.
ios.settings.notifications.detail.stalen: Raised after a couple of weeks without a completed sync while changes are still outstanding. Turning it off stops the warning only — syncing carries on as usual.
ios.settings.recovery.escrow.footer: Your recovery phrase is the only way back in if you lose every device. Nobody, including your server, can recover your library without it.
ios.settings.recovery.escrow.label: Recovery
ios.settings.recovery.minted.footer: Shown once. Write it down or save it to your password manager before you dismiss this — nobody can show it to you again.
ios.settings.recovery.minted.label: Recovery phrase
ios.settings.recovery.restore.confirm.me: Capsule will reconcile this device against what your phrase unlocks. The four rules above say exactly what happens to each photo.
ios.settings.recovery.restore.footer: A restore never overwrites newer work on this device. Anything that disagrees is held for you to decide.
ios.settings.recovery.verify.footer: A check every so often catches a phrase that was written down wrong. It never blocks anything.
ios.settings.recovery.verify.rewrap_offe: After several unsuccessful checks, Capsule can give you a new phrase for the same account key. Your photos aren't touched.
ios.settings.report.footer: Builds a redacted report — recent logs, device info, and the last crash. No photos or album contents are included. You choose where to send it.
ios.settings.security.atrest.sandbox.sum: No other app can reach Capsule's files, and the whole device is encrypted when it's locked.
ios.settings.security.atrest.store.label: Stored In
ios.settings.security.atrest.userdir.pro: Protected by whatever protects your Mac
ios.settings.security.atrest.userdir.sto: A folder in your home directory
ios.settings.security.atrest.userdir.sum: On a Mac the library is an ordinary folder you can open. Anything running as you can read it, so turn on FileVault if you haven't.
ios.settings.security.capture.label: Screenshots
ios.settings.security.gate.cancelled: You cancelled the last unlock, so nothing was unlocked.
ios.settings.security.gate.footer: Each view unlocks on its own and locks itself again after a while. Unlocking one never unlocks the other.
ios.settings.security.method.footer: Capsule uses whatever this device already offers. There's no separate Capsule passcode to forget.
ios.settings.security.method.label: Unlock Method
ios.settings.security.method.unavailable: Nothing set — these views can't be locked
ios.settings.security.plaintext.body: Photos you're looking at, previews, and search indexes exist unsealed on this device — that's what makes them fast to open. Your server only ever receives sealed copies.
ios.settings.security.plaintext.footer: Everything that leaves this device is sealed first.
ios.settings.server.connection.label: Connection
ios.settings.server.empty.description: Capsule is running on this device only. Connect a server to back up and sync.
ios.settings.server.empty.title: No Server
ios.settings.server.origin.footer: Your photos live here when they're not on this device.
ios.settings.server.portability.body: You can move to a different server and keep your identity and your photos. Your old handle keeps pointing at the new one, so people you share with follow along.
ios.settings.server.version.footer: Capsule and your server have to agree on the protocol version. If they stop agreeing, updating the app is the fix.
ios.settings.state.empty.description: There's nothing to configure here yet.
ios.settings.state.empty.title: Nothing to Show
ios.settings.state.error.title: Something Went Wrong
ios.settings.state.offline.description: Some settings need your server. What you can see is the last it told this device.
ios.settings.state.offline.title: No Connection
ios.settings.storage.budget.footer: Capsule clears the oldest downloaded copies first when it goes over. Anything cleared is fetched again when you need it.
ios.settings.storage.budget.label: Keep At Most
ios.settings.storage.evict.confirm.messa: Capsule downloads these again when you need them. Nothing is removed from your server.
ios.settings.storage.evict.confirm.title: Clear Cached Copies?
ios.settings.storage.local.footer: Clearing space here doesn't change what's stored on your server.
ios.settings.storage.local.unreleased: Not Yet Stored on Your Server
ios.settings.storage.quota.footer: Deleted photos still count until they're purged for good.
ios.settings.storage.quota.label: Status
ios.settings.storage.reclaim.footer: Only copies your server already holds are cleared. Anything it hasn't confirmed stays put.

ios.settings.subtitle.federation: Other servers and what you accept from them
ios.settings.subtitle.security: Unlocking hidden photos and how your library is stored
ios.settings.subtitle.server: Your home server, its version, and moving away
ios.settings.subtitle.storage: Space used here and on your server
ios.settings.subtitle.sync: What syncs, and on which connections
ios.settings.sync.force.confirm.message: Capsule will transfer everything outstanding on your current connection, cellular included. This can use a lot of data.
ios.settings.sync.force.confirm.title: Sync on This Connection?
ios.settings.sync.policy.footer: Either way, the copy on this device is kept until your server confirms it holds the full-size photo.
ios.settings.sync.policy.label: Upload
ios.settings.sync.scope.footer: Full-size photos are always fetched on demand when you open or share one, whatever you choose here.
ios.settings.sync.scope.label: Fetch
ios.settings.sync.stale.footer: The system decides when Capsule may work in the background, and sometimes it doesn't for a while. This is how you find out.
ios.settings.sync.status.footer: Capsule reads changes in order, so an interrupted sync picks up where it stopped.
ios.settings.upload.footer: Optionally send diagnostic reports to your own Capsule server. Off by default — Capsule never sends anything to a third party.
ios.share.composer.passphrase.footer: Send the passphrase separately from the link. Anyone with both can open it.
ios.share.composer.title: Share Link
ios.share.issued.footer: The key to this link is in the address itself, so anyone you send it to can open it. Your server never sees that key.
ios.share.list.empty.description: Links you create will be listed here, so you can see and revoke them.
ios.share.list.empty.title: No Shared Links
ios.share.list.revoke.confirm_message: Anyone holding it will stop being able to open it, within a minute. Your photos aren't affected.
ios.share.list.section.record_footer: Kept so you can see what you shared and when. These links no longer open anything.
ios.share.list.title: Shared Links
ios.share.offline_notice: Offline — this list may be out of date
ios.share.privacy.footer: Capsule removes these every time a shared photo is served. Nothing here is optional.
ios.share.privacy.no_opt_out: There's no way to turn this off for a share link.
ios.share.scope.album_wide: This link opens the whole album, including photos added later
ios.share.scope.no_analytics: You'll see that the link was used, not who used it.
ios.share.scope.read_only: Recipients can look, not change anything.
ios.share.scope.revocation_delay: Revoking takes effect within a minute.
ios.share.state.error.title: Something Went Wrong
ios.share.state.offline.description: Capsule needs your server to create or change a link.
ios.share.state.offline.title: No Connection
ios.storage.budget.footer: Capsule keeps downloaded copies up to this limit and clears the oldest first when it goes over.
ios.storage.budget.title: Keep At Most
ios.storage.budget.unset: No limit set yet — Capsule is managing this on its own.
ios.storage.consumer.trash.note: Emptying Recently Deleted frees this space.
ios.storage.consumers.footer: Grouped by kind rather than by photo — Capsule tracks these figures in bulk, not per picture.
ios.storage.empty.description: Capsule couldn't read how much space it's using on this device.
ios.storage.empty.title: No Storage Information
ios.storage.exempt.footer: These are the only copies. Capsule won't clear them until your server confirms it has each one.
ios.storage.free_up.confirm.message: Capsule will download these again when you need them. Nothing is removed from your server.
ios.storage.free_up.confirm.title: Clear Cached Copies?
ios.storage.free_up.footer: Anything cleared here is downloaded again when you need it, as long as your server has it.
ios.storage.link.quota.footer: Clearing space here doesn't change what's stored on your server.
ios.storage.plan.exempt: Some copies are held back because your server hasn't confirmed it has them
ios.storage.plan.refetch_note: Cleared in this order: full-size photos first, thumbnails last. Anything cleared is fetched again when you need it.
ios.storage.plan.shortfall: This won't get all the way under your limit
ios.storage.title: Space on This Device
ios.sync.action.footer.deferred: Large transfers are waiting for a better connection. Sync Now Anyway goes ahead regardless.
ios.sync.action.footer.unmetered: This connection allows everything, including full-size photos.
ios.sync.auto.footer: Automatic sync runs when the system gives Capsule time in the background.
ios.sync.auto.staleness_warning: Warn Me If This Device Falls Behind
ios.sync.criteria.footer: These decide when work runs on its own. Sync Now Anyway ignores them.

ios.sync.criterion.external_power.descri: Very large batches wait until this device is charging.
ios.sync.criterion.non_metered.descripti: Details and previews sync on any connection that isn't cellular.
ios.sync.cursor.footer: Capsule reads changes from your server in order, so an interrupted sync picks up exactly where it stopped.
ios.sync.empty.description: This device is up to date with your server.
ios.sync.empty.title: Nothing to Sync
ios.sync.policy.footer: Either way, your local copy is kept until the full-size photo is safely stored on your server.
ios.sync.policy.full.description: Uploads the full-size photo along with everything else, as soon as the connection allows.
ios.sync.policy.staged.description: Sends details and previews first, so photos appear on your other devices quickly, and the full-size file when Wi-Fi is available.
ios.sync.scope.empty.description: Connect a server to choose what this device keeps.
ios.sync.scope.empty.title: Nothing to Configure
ios.sync.scope.footer: Full-size photos are always fetched on demand when you open or share one, whatever you choose here.

ios.sync.scope.originals.description: Keeps a full-size copy of every photo on this device. Uses the most space.
ios.sync.scope.thumbnails.description: Adds thumbnails and preview-sized copies, so browsing looks right without keeping full-size files.
ios.sync.scope.title: What to Sync
ios.sync.scope.unknown.description: A setting a newer version of Capsule wrote. It's kept exactly as it is.
ios.sync.snooze.footer: You won't be reminded again for a couple of weeks. Syncing carries on as usual in the meantime.
ios.sync.stale.description: Capsule hasn't finished a sync in two weeks, and there are still changes to send. On this device the system decides when background work runs, and it hasn't granted any.
